"""A tiny chat protocol (the kind of code the TCP-chat assignment asks for): commands, unique nicknames, message
framing. It is the KNOWN-GOOD version; the variants in ../variants/ each break it in one labelled way."""

import threading

MAX_NICK = 16


class ProtocolError(ValueError):
    pass


def parse_command(line: str) -> tuple[str, list[str]]:
    """'/nick Ada' -> ('nick', ['Ada']); '/msg Bob hi there' -> ('msg', ['Bob', 'hi there']);
    plain text -> ('say', [text])."""
    line = line.strip()
    if not line.startswith("/"):
        return "say", [line]
    name, _, rest = line[1:].partition(" ")
    name = name.lower()
    if name == "nick":
        return "nick", [rest.strip()]
    if name == "msg":
        target, _, text = rest.strip().partition(" ")
        if not target or not text:
            raise ProtocolError("usage: /msg <nick> <text>")
        return "msg", [target, text]
    if name == "quit":
        return "quit", []
    raise ProtocolError(f"unknown command /{name}")


class NicknameRegistry:
    """Unique nicknames across client threads (case-insensitive)."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._names: dict[str, str] = {}
        self._lock = threading.Lock()

    def register(self, client_id: str, nick: str) -> bool:
        if not nick or len(nick) > MAX_NICK or not nick.isalnum():
            raise ProtocolError("a nickname is 1-16 letters or digits")
        with self._lock:
            key = nick.lower()
            if key in self._names:
                return False
            self._names[key] = client_id
            return True

    def unregister(self, nick: str) -> None:
        with self._lock:
            self._names.pop(nick.lower(), None)

    def __len__(self) -> int:
        return len(self._names)


def frame(message: str) -> bytes
    """Length-prefixed frame: 4-byte big-endian length + UTF-8 body."""
    body = message.encode("utf-8")
    return len(body).to_bytes(4, "big") + body


def unframe(buffer: bytes) -> tuple[list[str], bytes]:
    """Every complete message in ``buffer`` and the incomplete rest (TCP may split or join frames)."""
    messages = []
    while len(buffer) >= 4:
        size = int.from_bytes(buffer[:4], "big")
        if len(buffer) < 4 + size:
            break
        messages.append(buffer[4:4 + size].decode("utf-8"))
        buffer = buffer[4 + size:]
    return messages, buffer

"""Tests for chatproto.py: run against the good version (all pass) and against each variant (each must fail in its
labelled way)."""

import threading

import pytest
from chatproto import NicknameRegistry, ProtocolError, frame, parse_command, unframe


def test_plain_text_is_said() -> None:
    assert parse_command("hello all") == ("say", ["hello all"])


def test_commands_are_parsed_case_insensitively() -> None:
    assert parse_command("/NICK Ada") == ("nick", ["Ada"])
    assert parse_command("/msg Bob hi there") == ("msg", ["Bob", "hi there"])
    assert parse_command("/quit") == ("quit", [])


def test_bad_commands_are_rejected() -> None:
    with pytest.raises(ProtocolError):
        parse_command("/msg Bob")
    with pytest.raises(ProtocolError):
        parse_command("/dance")


def test_nicknames_are_unique_case_insensitively() -> None:
    reg = NicknameRegistry()
    assert reg.register("c1", "Ada")
    assert not reg.register("c2", "ada")
    reg.unregister("ADA")
    assert reg.register("c2", "ada") and len(reg) == 1


def test_invalid_nicknames_are_refused() -> None:
    reg = NicknameRegistry()
    for bad in ["", "a" * 17, "no spaces"]:
        with pytest.raises(ProtocolError):
            reg.register("c1", bad)


def test_only_one_thread_gets_a_contested_nickname() -> None:
    reg = NicknameRegistry()
    wins = []
    start = threading.Barrier(20)

    def grab(i: int) -> None:
        start.wait()
        if reg.register(f"c{i}", "popular"):
            wins.append(i)

    threads = [threading.Thread(target=grab, args=(i,)) for i in range(20)]
    for t in threads:
        t.start()
    for t in threads:
        t.join()
    assert len(wins) == 1


def test_frames_round_trip_split_and_joined() -> None:
    data = frame("hi") + frame("héllo wörld") + frame("x")
    msgs, rest = unframe(data)
    assert msgs == ["hi", "héllo wörld", "x"] and rest == b""
    first, rest = unframe(data[:5])
    assert first == [] and rest == data[:5]                       # an incomplete frame waits for more bytes
    msgs, rest = unframe(rest + data[5:])
    assert msgs == ["hi", "héllo wörld", "x"]


def test_frame_header_is_the_byte_length() -> None:
    assert frame("é")[:4] == (2).to_bytes(4, "big")
